# RETRO: PR #13159 (team 2)

## What worked
- Asking both reviewers to read upstream source at the versions reported in the issue (Chrome 154, Quickshell 0.3.1, libnotify) settled the central question. Both independently found that the PR's Chromium rationale is wrong.
- Cross-examination with one neutral question each turned the two single-sourced claims (multi-screen hover; the first-party sender inventory) into claims confirmed by both reviewers, without sharing either reviewer's conclusions.
- Source-only scope was enough. No desktop resources were needed.

## Friction
- `node` is not available inside the review.py sandbox, so the Opus reviewer's prepared test and mutation fixture could not run, and test-survival claims remain source-established only. Feature request for the toolkit: provide a sandbox-visible Node (for example an approved copy in a shared fixture location) so Node-based shell tests and mutation checks can run.
- The harness auto-loads the pinned worktree's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` whenever an agent reads files there (this happened to both the Opus reviewer and the coordinator). It was treated as untrusted data. Consider a sandboxed copy location or a supported setting that suppresses auto-loading of project instructions for the reviewed tree.

## Process deviations (recorded, not publication-blocking)
- Opus reviewer (self-reported in opus/final.md retrospective): several single reads of 53-64 lines and parallel read batches of up to 105 lines exceeded the 50/60-line bounds, with nothing truncated; one grep used `cut -c1-200` (it matched nothing); `head -c` was used on a small receipt; one `git log` ran without `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. The follow-up stayed within bounds. None affects the public claims, which rest on content that was read in full and on independent Sol confirmation.
- Coordinator: the PR diff was read in two chunks (50 and 53 lines), and the second exceeded the 50-content-line target but stayed under the 60-line aggregate. One Service.qml read was 48 lines. The Opus dispatch prompt used the exact wording required by the runtime section; the first-call rules were placed at the top of the 50-line brief rather than in the prompt itself. This differs from the older PR13009 guidance, which puts them in the dispatch message.
- Opus follow-up via SendMessage and Sol follow-up via `pi_job resume`: both answer files appeared on the first send.

## Carry forward
- When a PR's rationale describes another project's behavior, name that project's source at the reported version in the brief. That was decisive here.
- For UI code built on `Variants` over screens, ask whether per-delegate state such as timers or hover is duplicated across outputs.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change gives the payload reported in #13153 (`app "Google Chrome"`, urgency critical, `expire_timeout` 0) a finite popup lifetime, and Omarchy's own critical toasts keep their permanent popup. The one substantive issue is the stated reason for the change: Chromium does not mark every web notification critical, so the docs and code comment describe a different trade-off from the one the code makes.

| Sender and shape | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `Google Chrome`, critical, expire 0 (the issue's payload) | stays until dismissed | 8 s |
| `Google Chrome`, normal, expire -1 (ordinary web notification) | 8 s | 8 s (unchanged) |
| `omarchy-action`, critical (Omarchy's own toasts) | stays | stays |
| `notify-send` without `-a`, critical | stays | stays |
| Other app name, critical, expire 20000 / 60000 | stays | 20 s / 30 s (cap) |
| Restored after restart: Chrome critical persisted more than 8 s earlier | shown again, stays | archived to history |

**Verified:** both `durationFor` call sites (live card and `restorePopups`) pass the app name. DND decisions, low and normal durations, and the countdown restart on content updates are unchanged. `notify-send` without `-a` sends the app name `notify-send` (libnotify `notify_init("notify-send")`).

### Chromium marks a notification critical only when the page sets `requireInteraction`

The PR description, `docs/notifications.md` and the new comment in `NotificationLogic.js` state that Chromium stamps critical urgency on every web notification. In the Chrome 154.0.8037.57 Linux notification bridge, that happens only for notifications that should never time out:

```text
page: showNotification(title, { requireInteraction: true })
  -> set_never_timeout(true)                  platform_notification_service_impl.cc
  -> urgency CRITICAL, expire_timeout 0       notification_platform_bridge_linux.cc
     (on every server except KDE Plasma and wf-panel-pi; Quickshell reports "quickshell")

page: showNotification(title, {})              default
  -> urgency NORMAL, expire_timeout -1         already expires after 8 s on the base branch
```

Sources: [bridge](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/154.0.8037.57/chrome/browser/notifications/notification_platform_bridge_linux.cc#L1007-L1062), [web notification construction](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/154.0.8037.57/chrome/browser/notifications/platform_notification_service_impl.cc#L640-L648).

**Impact:** the fix still resolves the reported payload. However, a reader of the docs would conclude that no Chrome notification expires without this rule, and would not see that the rule overrides pages that explicitly asked to keep a notification until the user acts. When such a toast expires, Chromium reports it to the page as closed. The manual YouTube/Teams check in the PR description exercises the change only if that site sets `requireInteraction`; ordinary web notifications expired after 8 s before this PR too.

**Suggested change:** reword the docs and the code comment along these lines: "Chromium marks a web notification critical, with `expire_timeout` 0, when the page sets `requireInteraction`, so a critical toast from any other app name gets the normal 8s lifetime (or its requested `expire_timeout`, capped at 30s) instead." It may also help to note that the rule applies to every sender except `omarchy-action` and bare `notify-send`, so user scripts using a custom `--app-name` or `notify-send -a` with critical urgency also lose the permanent popup (the toast still moves to history).

**Pre-existing, now more visible:** with more than one screen, each screen renders its own copy of every toast with its own countdown and hover state, and expiry removes the shared row. Hovering a toast on one screen does not stop the copy on another screen from expiring it. Low and normal toasts on the base branch already behave this way; this PR extends it to third-party critical toasts. A fix (one countdown per row, or pausing every copy while any copy is hovered) would be a separate change.

**Optional test improvement:** the five new assertions call `keepsCriticalOnScreen` directly, and no test references `durationFor` or its two call sites. By source inspection, dropping the app argument at either call site would make Omarchy's own critical toasts expire after 8 s (or be archived on restart) with the suite still passing. Two source assertions in the file's existing `Service.qml` regex style, one per call site, would catch that.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head and base, plus upstream Chromium 154.0.8037.57, Quickshell 0.3.1 and libnotify notification sources. No repository tests, shell or GUI were run, and multi-screen behavior was not observed on real outputs. Which web apps (including Teams) set `requireInteraction` was not verified.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
